# Design: Factory Monitor Dashboard - Phase 1B: Detailed Contracts

**Feature Name**: factory-monitor-dashboard
**Date**: 2026-09-23
**Status**: Phase 1B - API Contracts & Integration Points
**Version**: 1.0
**Author**: Generated by @monkeymode

---

## Scope Note

This is a client-only SPA against a **pre-built, unmodified mock backend** (MSW REST handlers + a simulated WebSocket). There is no new server, no auth, no versioning, and no database — so several template sections from the standard Phase 1B guide (Authentication & Authorization, Pagination, Rate Limiting, API Versioning, Load/Performance Testing with k6-style tools, Events Published) are **not applicable** and are marked as such below rather than silently omitted. What this phase actually contracts is: (1) the existing backend surface this feature *consumes*, documented precisely because two of its endpoints have real data-quality bugs the frontend must defend against, and (2) the **new frontend contracts** this feature introduces — hook signatures and pure functions everything else is built on.

---

## Part 1: Consumed Backend Contracts (existing, unmodified, read-only reference)

### Authentication & Authorization
Not applicable — mock backend, no auth in this exercise (PRT §7).

### Common Error Responses
MSW handlers return either the requested JSON or a bare `404` (no structured error body) for `GET /api/machines/:machineId` (unknown id) and `POST /api/alerts/:alertId/acknowledge` (unknown id — this is exactly the case hit by `ws-alt-*` ids, see ADR-001). All hooks must treat a non-2xx as `isError`/mutation `onError` — there is no error `code`/`message` payload to parse.

### Endpoints Consumed

| Method | Path | Consumed by | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/factory/status` | `useFactoryStatus()` (polls every 30s) | Computed fresh per call: `{connected, totalMachines, zoneCount, uptimeHours, lastUpdated}` |
| GET | `/api/zones` | `useZones()` | Returns all 4 zones with `health` |
| GET | `/api/zones/:zoneId/machines` | **new** `useAllMachines()` (fanned out via `useQueries`, one call per zone from `useZones()`) | No "all machines" endpoint exists; this is the only way to get all 14 |
| GET | `/api/alerts?severity=&zone=` | `useAlerts(filters)` | Filters the mock's in-memory alerts array; does **not** include WebSocket-originated alerts |
| POST | `/api/alerts/:alertId/acknowledge` | `useAcknowledgeAlert()` | Mutates in-memory state; `invalidateQueries(["alerts"])` on success (see ADR-001 for why live alerts must never live in this cache key); 404s for any id the mock doesn't recognize, including `ws-alt-*` |

**Fields with known defects (must be defended against, not "fixed" — mock is out of scope for edits):**
- `alt-004.machine_name` (snake_case) instead of `machineName`
- `alt-005.timestamp` = `"1969-12-31T23:59:59Z"` (invalid/garbage)
- `alt-006.zoneId` = `"assembly"` but `.zoneName` = `"Welding Bay"` (mismatched)

### Caching Strategy (existing, unchanged)
TanStack Query defaults set in `App.tsx`: `staleTime: 10000`, `retry: 1`. `useFactoryStatus` additionally sets `refetchInterval: 30000`. This feature does not change these; `useAllMachines` (new) inherits the same `QueryClient` defaults.

### Pagination / Rate Limiting / Versioning
Not applicable — all list endpoints return their full dataset (max 50 in the stress scenario), no auth means no per-client rate limiting, and there is exactly one API consumer (this app) so no versioning concern exists.

## Part 2: Events Consumed (WebSocket)

The mock WebSocket (`src/mocks/websocket.ts`, `MockWebSocketServer` singleton, exposed to the app via `useFactoryWebSocket(onMessage)`) emits two message types. **Consumed only — this app publishes nothing.**

#### `telemetry`
**Frequency:** ~every 3000ms, one random machine per tick
**Payload (does NOT match the `Machine` type — no `status` field):**
```json
{
  "type": "telemetry",
  "payload": {
    "machineId": "string",
    "machineName": "string",
    "zoneId": "string",
    "telemetry": { "temperature": "number", "vibration": "number", "throughput": "number", "powerDraw": "number" },
    "timestamp": "ISO8601"
  }
}
```
**Consumer:** `LiveProvider` → stores as `TelemetrySnapshot` keyed by `machineId`, overwriting the previous value. Never mutates a machine's `status`.

#### `alert`
**Frequency:** ~every 15000ms, ~30% chance per tick, one random machine + random severity
**Payload (known defect: `zoneName` is set to the raw `zoneId`, not the human-readable zone name):**
```json
{
  "type": "alert",
  "payload": {
    "id": "ws-alt-{timestamp}",
    "machineId": "string", "machineName": "string",
    "zoneId": "string", "zoneName": "string (BUG: actually the zoneId)",
    "severity": "critical | warning | info",
    "message": "string", "timestamp": "ISO8601", "acknowledged": false
  }
}
```
**Consumer:** `LiveProvider` → appended to `liveAlerts` (functional `setState`, deduped by `id`). `zoneName` is discarded and re-resolved from `zoneId` via `useZones()` by `normalizeAlert` — never trusted from this payload (same treatment as `alt-006`'s mismatch).

**Delivery guarantee:** none — these are timer-fired, at-most-once, in-memory events with no replay if a listener wasn't subscribed. `LiveProvider` subscribes exactly once for the app's lifetime (mounted in `App.tsx`), so no messages are missed after initial load.

### External Service Dependencies / Dependency Analysis
Not applicable beyond the single mock backend described above — no other services, no circuit breakers, no SLAs (this is a self-contained demo app).

## Part 3: New Frontend Contracts (this feature)

These are the actual "API" this design introduces — TypeScript function/hook signatures every story in Phase 2 is built against. Full bodies are Phase 3 (Code Spec); this phase fixes the **shape**.

### `src/lib/status.ts`
```ts
export const severityColor: Record<Alert["severity"], string>;      // critical→"red", warning→"orange", info→"blue"
export const healthColor: Record<Zone["health"], string>;           // healthy→"green", degraded→"orange", faulted→"red"
export const machineStatusColor: Record<Machine["status"], string>; // running→"green", idle→"gray", error→"red", maintenance→"purple"
```

### `src/lib/alerts.ts`
```ts
export interface NormalizedAlert extends Alert {
  zoneName: string;       // always resolved via zoneById, never the raw field
  machineName: string;    // machineName ?? machine_name ?? machineId
  timestampValid: boolean;
  source: "rest" | "live";
}
export function normalizeAlert(raw: Alert & { machine_name?: string }, zoneById: Map<string, Zone>, source: "rest" | "live"): NormalizedAlert;
export function sortAlerts(alerts: NormalizedAlert[]): NormalizedAlert[]; // unacked first, then severity desc, then newest; invalid timestamps sort last within their group
export function dedupeById(alerts: NormalizedAlert[]): NormalizedAlert[];

export interface MachineAlertGroup {
  machineId: string; machineName: string; zoneId: string; zoneName: string;
  alerts: NormalizedAlert[]; worstSeverity: Alert["severity"]; unacknowledgedCount: number;
}
export function groupByMachine(alerts: NormalizedAlert[]): MachineAlertGroup[]; // sorted worst-severity-first, then most recent
export function formatRelativeTime(iso: string): string; // "Unknown time" for invalid/pre-2000 timestamps, else "Ns ago"/"Nm ago"/"Nh ago"
```

### `src/hooks/useAllMachines.ts`
```ts
export function useAllMachines(): {
  machines: Machine[] | undefined;
  isLoading: boolean;
  isError: boolean;
};
// Implementation: useZones() → useQueries({ queries: zones.map(z => ({ queryKey: ["machines", z.id], queryFn: () => fetch(`/api/zones/${z.id}/machines`) })) }) → flatMap results
```

### `src/live/LiveProvider.tsx`
```ts
export interface LiveContextValue {
  liveAlerts: NormalizedAlert[];        // raw, not yet merged with REST — merging happens in useActiveAlerts
  telemetry: Record<string, TelemetrySnapshot>;
  lastMessageAt: number | null;         // Date.now() of the most recent WS message, any type
  localAckIds: Set<string>;
  acknowledgeLocal: (id: string) => void;
}
export function LiveProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element;
export function useLive(): LiveContextValue; // throws if used outside LiveProvider
```
**Contract constraint (from ADR-001 in 1a-discovery.md):** `LiveProvider` calls `useFactoryWebSocket` exactly once, at the App root. Its `onMessage` callback uses only functional `setState` updates (`setLiveAlerts(prev => ...)`) because the underlying hook's effect has `[]` deps and captures the callback once.

### `src/hooks/useActiveAlerts.ts`
```ts
export function useActiveAlerts(filters?: { severity?: Alert["severity"]; zone?: string }): {
  alerts: NormalizedAlert[];            // REST ∪ live, deduped, normalized, sorted
  isLoading: boolean;
  isError: boolean;
  acknowledge: (id: string) => void;    // routes ws-alt-* to local ack, else useAcknowledgeAlert().mutate
  acknowledgePending: boolean;
  bulkAcknowledge: (ids: string[]) => Promise<{ succeeded: string[]; failed: string[] }>;
};
```
**Contract constraint:** client-side `severity`/`zone` filtering is applied to the *merged* set (REST filters only affect the REST call; live alerts are filtered identically in-memory so a filtered view is consistent regardless of an alert's origin).

## Testing Strategy

**No test runner is installed in this repo** (`package.json` has no `test` script, no vitest/jest/testing-library dependency) — confirmed during Phase 1A discovery. Adding one is out of scope for this exercise (PRT §3, "Out of Scope"). The testing strategy is therefore **manual verification**, formalized as an explicit acceptance checklist in Phase 2B rather than skipped:

- **Static verification:** `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) must pass with zero errors before each commit — this is the only automated gate available and catches contract mismatches (e.g. a component destructuring a field `useActiveAlerts` doesn't return).
- **Manual functional verification:** every Must/Should acceptance criterion in the PRT (§5) is walked through in the browser at `http://localhost:5173`, using `window.__setAlertScenario("empty"|"stress"|"default")` to exercise the 0-alert and 50-alert edge cases the mock provides for exactly this purpose.
- **Design-for-testability (even without a runner):** `src/lib/alerts.ts` and `src/lib/status.ts` are written as pure functions with no React/hook dependencies specifically so they *could* be unit tested if a runner is added later — this is a structural choice made now, not deferred work.
- **Mock boundaries if tests were added later:** `mockWebSocket`'s timers and `Math.random()` would need seeding/mocking; MSW handlers already provide a natural network-boundary mock.
- **Integration/Contract/Load testing:** Not applicable — no real network boundary, no other consumers of this app, and alert volume (max ~50 in the provided stress fixture) does not warrant load testing.
- **End-to-end critical journeys:** the five journeys enumerated in `ux-ideation.md` ("Factory Overview at a glance", "Spot the top problem and act", "Triage a bad day", "Zone health drives attention", "Real-time awareness") are the E2E scope, executed manually per the Phase 7 acceptance checklist.
